equity_bridge.item: PACCAR Financial Services equity at segment book value (assets 22,265.5 less liabilities 16,291.1, 2026-06-30, 10-Q segment balance sheet)
equity_bridge.note: Captive lender funded by its own 14,696.4 of commercial paper and term notes, all of which are inside this net figure. Held at 1.0x book in all scenarios; each 0.1x of P/B is ~$1.13/share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: 10-year base-case industrial revenue CAGR (FY2025 trough 26,235 to FY2035 ~37,800), built from a ~2-3% nominal heavy-truck market trend, 4-8% Parts growth and management's 30% to 35% North American share target, with a 2027 post-EPA air pocket inside the path
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (13.5% 3yr / 12.8% 5yr) diverges by >30% from revenue CAGR (-0.4% 3yr) and EPS CAGR (-7.8% 3yr). Book value compounded through the FY2022-24 up-cycle on retained peak earnings (ROE 26% in FY2024) while revenue and EPS have since fallen from the FY2023 peak; the equity CAGR describes the last cycle's retained earnings, not forward growth, and is NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are on CONSOLIDATED CSV data (FY2022->FY2025 for 3yr, FY2020->FY2025 for 5yr) and are cycle-position artefacts: FY2020 is a COVID trough, FY2022 is mid-recovery, FY2025 is a freight-recession trough. FCF CAGRs use reported FCF less SBC (FY2020 1,316.7; FY2022 1,639.4; FY2025 3,648.7) and are additionally distorted by (a) the consolidated series including Financial Services operating cash, (b) the capex line including operating-lease equipment purchases before FY2025 and PP&E only in FY2025, and (c) a large industrial working-capital release in the FY2025 down year. Investment income is not available for FY2020/FY2022 in the extracted data so the owner-FCF history is SBC-adjusted only. None of these CAGRs are used to set growth; the base path is a mid-cycle judgment.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle. The freight recession bottomed in FY2025 (industrial EBITDA margin 11.2%); H2 2026 recovers on EPA27 pre-buy and tariff clarity (Q3 deliveries ~42k), 2027 dips modestly after the regulation change, and FY2028-29 carry a normal replacement up-cycle. Margins mature at 13.8%, a little above the 2018-25 average because Parts (a ~25%-margin annuity on the installed base, 26% of industrial revenue and growing 4-8%) keeps gaining weight. Financial Services is worth its $6.0B book. The $8.7B cash pile is counted once, as cash, with its $346M of investment income stripped from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: A real multi-year up-cycle: US Class 8 runs at the top of the 230-270k range through the pre-buy, the post-EPA27 dip is shallow because fleets are under-replaced after four weak years, Kenworth/Peterbilt take North American share toward 35% on the Section 232 domestic-manufacturing edge, and DAF rides the European recovery. Industrial margins settle at the FY2024 level (15%) rather than the 2018-25 average, i.e. the market's current optimism about structural margin improvement is right.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 pre-buy is followed by a 2007/2010-style cliff in 2027 that lands on a renewed freight recession; EPA27 content inflates cost per truck faster than price; tariff policy flips against PACCAR; Financial Services credit costs rise (provision already 124.5 in FY2025 from 31.3 in FY2023). Margins trough near 9.5% and recover only to 12.5% as the scaled global peers compete for volume. Equity value is still well supported by $8.7B of industrial net cash and FS book, so the bear is an earnings story, not a balance-sheet one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PACCAR is a high-quality cyclical: best-in-class residual values, a growing parts annuity that earns most of the profit at the trough, a debt-free industrial balance sheet with $8.7B of cash and securities, and a conservatively capitalised captive lender. The valuation refuses to capitalise either the FY2023-24 pricing peak or the FY2025 trough: it values the industrial business on a mid-cycle margin path at a 9% cost of equity with a 14x owner-FCF terminal cap, adds the cash once, and adds Financial Services at book. On that basis the stock is fully to somewhat richly priced; the market is paying for the up-cycle and for structural margin gains that the bull case, not the base case, delivers.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: a deeper or longer 2027 post-EPA27 air pocket than the base -2% (the bear's -12%) is the single largest swing factor in the explicit years.
Mid-cycle margin level: each 1pp on the terminal industrial EBITDA margin is roughly $7-8/share; the base 13.8% sits between the 2018-25 average (13%) and the FY2024 peak (15.7%).
Terminal multiple: the 14x owner-FCF cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 9%/2.5% would give 15.8x); a buyer paying 12x or 16x moves value by roughly -$7 / +$7 per share.

Financial Services carried at 1.0x book ($11.3/share): a credit-cycle writedown or a view that 6.5% ROE deserves 0.7x book takes ~$3.4/share off; FS also carries used-truck residual-value risk on $1.9B of operating-lease equipment.
Cash treated as fully surplus: PACCAR has historically run with $4-9B of cash through cycles; if $2-3B of it is operating liquidity rather than surplus, value is overstated by $4-6/share.
Tariff and trade policy: the IEEPA ruling, Section 232 truck tariffs and any retaliation against DAF exports can swing Truck margins by 1-2pp in either direction within a year.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 92.25-139.24
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (accession 0001193125-26-323642, filed 2026-07-29) for the segment balance sheet, H1 segment income, cash flow, diluted shares and 2026 outlook; 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001193125-26-057025, filed 2026-02-18) for the FY2023-25 segment data (revenue, pre-tax income, D&A, capex), investment income, EC litigation charges, SBC and tax; XBRL companyfacts for the quarterly tag history; research/PCAR/Reports/PCAR_Metrics.csv for the consolidated FY2007-Q2 2026 history. Extracted text saved to research/PCAR/Extracted/.
data_sources.qualitative: research/PCAR/Reports/PCAR_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): market shares, EPA27 pre-buy/air-pocket dynamics, Parts guidance, tariff position, consensus targets.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 Truck, Parts and Other net sales and revenues to external customers (10-K FY2025 segment note). EXCLUDES Financial Services revenue of 2,209.7 and investment income of 346.1; both are valued in the equity bridge, not in the flows.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted-average diluted shares (10-Q, Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income). 526.4M issued at 2026-06-30 plus dilutive options; 1.14M antidilutive options excluded. Held FLAT: SBC (0.09% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Truck, Parts and Other cash and cash equivalents 5,407.8 + marketable securities 3,259.6 at 2026-06-30 (10-Q segment balance sheet, also shown as 'Cash and marketable securities 8,667.4' in the segment-assets note). Industrial segment carries no borrowings. Financial Services debt (commercial paper and bank loans 4,788.9 + term notes 9,907.5 = 14,696.4) is EXCLUDED: it funds FS receivables and is netted inside the FS equity line in equity_bridge. No dividend payable outstanding at 2026-06-30.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 consolidated: operating cash flow 4,415.8 less payments for property, plant and equipment 743.0. CAUTION: this consolidated figure includes Financial Services operating cash (FS depreciation ~420, FS after-tax income ~380, provision 125, wholesale-receivable collections) and FY2025 industrial working-capital release in a down year. It is NOT the model's FY0 base. The model projects industrial owner FCF from components on base_revenue; a component build of FY2025 industrial owner FCF (underlying pre-tax 2,542 after adding back the 350 EC charge, less 22% tax, plus D&A 407.7, less capex 728.3) is roughly 1,660 before working capital.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 Stock Compensation Plans note / cash-flow add-back: Stock-based compensation 24.1 (FY2024 22.9, FY2023 21.2). No separate net-share-settlement tax withholding line exists in the financing section (the only equity line is +47.3 proceeds from stock compensation transactions), so the cash-flow figure is the complete charge.
inputs.interest_income_basis: FY2025 Investment income on the Truck, Parts and Other cash and marketable-securities pile (10-K income statement; FY2024 394.7, FY2023 292.2; H1-2026 166.4). It is reported below the segment line, so the EBITDA margin paths already exclude it; the matching asset (8,667.4 of cash and securities) is added as net cash. Recorded here to make last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income reconstructible.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchases of treasury stock 36.1 (H1-2026: 4.8). PACCAR returns cash through regular plus special dividends (2,267.1 paid in FY2025), not buybacks; the flat count is a modelling convention that costs almost nothing because SBC is 0.09% of revenue. Diluted count has drifted +0.2%/yr (525.0 FY2023 to 527.6 Q2-2026).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 92.25-139.24
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST, Oct-2026), ERP 4.75%, beta ~1.0 for a large-cap truck OEM -> cost of equity ~9.0%. The industrial segment has zero debt so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality, the 2027 post-EPA air pocket and tariff risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP; operating lease liabilities 62.9 at 2025-12-31 are immaterial (0.2% of revenue) and are left as operating cost inside EBITDA; no lease liabilities in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests. The Amplify Cell Technologies battery JV is equity-accounted inside Other noncurrent assets; its share of losses runs through Truck, Parts and Other 'Interest and other (income) expenses' and is therefore inside the historical margins. Not separately valued.
inputs.captive_finance_treatment: Sum-of-parts within the owner-FCF engine. (1) The DCF runs on Truck, Parts and Other only: base_revenue, EBITDA margins, D&A and capex are all from the segment note ex Financial Services. (2) Financial Services is a captive lender funded by its own debt; its value is carried in equity_bridge at segment book equity (assets 22,265.5 less liabilities 16,291.1 = 5,974.4 at 2026-06-30), i.e. 1.0x book. FS pre-tax income was 540.3 / 435.6 / 485.4 in FY2023-25 (~6.5% ROE on a conservatively capitalised book, FS debt/equity ~2.5x), so 1.0x book neither credits nor penalises the franchise value it adds to truck sales. (3) FS debt is excluded from net debt (it is inside the FS equity line) and FS income is excluded from the flows, so nothing is counted twice.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' + owner-fcf-adaptations), run on the industrial business with the captive finance arm valued separately at book in the equity bridge and summed. Fresh build, no prior DCF. MID-CYCLE FRAMING: FY2023 (industrial EBITDA margin 17.8% ex the 600 EC charge) and FY2024 (15.7%) were a supply-constrained pricing peak; FY2025 (11.2% ex the 350 EC charge) and H1-2026 (11.9%, Q2 12.7%) are the freight-recession trough. The 2018-2025 average industrial EBITDA margin is ~13%; Parts (24.5% EBITDA margin, 26% of industrial revenue and rising, guided +4-8%/yr) lifts the mix roughly 0.1-0.2pp a year, which is why the base case matures at 13.8% rather than 13.0%. Neither the FY2023 peak nor the FY2025 trough is extrapolated. One-offs excluded from the margin history: EC civil-litigation charges of 600 (FY2023) and 350 (Q1 FY2025) in Other, and the 14 winch-sale gain (FY2024). Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (-5% of the revenue change) because a manufacturer's receivables and inventory grow with sales; PACCAR's payables and accruals offset most but not all of it. Cash tax 22% flat: FY2025 effective rate 21.4% (21.7% adjusted), cash taxes paid 646.3 on pre-tax 3,023.5 = 21.4%; CAMT credit carryforwards do not expire. Terminal cap 14x owner FCF for a cyclical with net cash and a parts annuity (house range 12-15x); Gordon at 9%/2.5% is 15.8x, so the cap binds in every scenario. SBC is 0.09% of revenue so the house/street band is a few cents wide; band_position is reported but carries no information here.

bear.rationale: The 2026 pre-buy pulls forward demand and 2027 is a genuine post-regulation cliff (-12% industrial revenue, in line with a ~25% US Class 8 drop cushioned by Parts and Europe) coinciding with a renewed freight/industrial recession; EPA27 engine content raises cost per truck ahead of pricing; tariff policy turns against PACCAR (IEEPA ruling, retaliation on DAF exports). Margins trough at 9.5% (FY2020-21 was ~10%) and recover only to 12.5%, below the long-run average, as competition from scaled peers (Daimler Truck, Traton) caps pricing. Still no solvency risk: $8.7B industrial net cash and no industrial debt.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7%: H1 industrial revenue was -4.6% y/y (13,231 vs 13,877) but Q3 deliveries are guided to ~42,000 from 38,700 in Q2 (and ~34,000 in Q3 2025) as the EPA27 pre-buy and tariff clarity lift build rates, so H2 runs ~+20% y/y. FY2027 -2%: the post-EPA27 air pocket in US Class 8 is offset by Europe's recovery and Parts +4-8%; the pre-buy is modest (industry guide 230-270k vs 232.8k in 2025) so the drop is far shallower than 2007/2010. FY2028-29 +8%/+6%: replacement cycle after four down years. Then fades to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 12.4%: H1 11.9%, Q2 12.7% on price realisation and lower tariff costs, H2 volume leverage. FY2027 12.0% on the volume dip. Matures at 13.8% by FY2030: 2018-25 average ~13% plus Parts mix shift (Parts 24.5% EBITDA margin, growing faster than Truck). Deliberately below the 15.7-17.8% of FY2023-24, which was a supply-constrained pricing peak.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guide $700-750M on ~28,100 industrial revenue = 2.6%; FY2023-25 actual 2.05%/2.6%/2.8% during the EPA27 engine, BEV and Mississippi/Eindhoven capacity programme. Fades to 2.1% as the programme completes; D&A (1.55% FY2025) rises toward 1.9% as the enlarged PP&E base depreciates, leaving a 0.2pp growth-capex gap at 2.5% terminal growth.

bull.rationale: Strong pre-buy into EPA27 (US Class 8 toward the 270k top of guidance), no 2027 air pocket worth the name because replacement demand is pent up, NA share climbs toward the stated 35% target on the domestic-manufacturing tariff edge, Europe (DAF ~30% share) recovers. Margins settle at 15%, i.e. the FY2024 level becomes the new mid-cycle because Parts keeps compounding at 6-8% and in-house powertrain/transmission content sticks.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the 2027 post-EPA27 air pocket is a dated, historically reliable event (2002, 2007, 2010) rather than a vague downside, and the Analysis JSON rates freight-cycle and 2027-regulation risk 'high'; it is not raised further because there is no solvency, covenant or single-customer dependency ($8.7B net cash, no industrial debt, no customer >5% of the FS book). Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things at once (a strong pre-buy with no hangover, share gain to 35%, and margins holding the FY2024 peak as the new mid-cycle), and Wall Street consensus is already Hold-leaning with targets clustered at $122-141, so the bull is partly priced.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
